title: I was sent to perfect character
hook: the Prophet ﷺ said he was sent to perfect good character

segments.voice: Yesterday, the theology close, and your line: believe, and live it. Today a new block begins: the inward path and good character.

Ask a room why a prophet is sent, and the answers come fast. To bring a law. To call people to worship one God. To warn, to give good news. All of those are in the Qur'an. But in one hadith the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, sums up his mission in a way that can catch a listener off guard. Not with law, not with ritual. With character.
screen: `WHY IS A PROPHET SENT?` → `LAW, WORSHIP, WARNING.` → `AND THEN: CHARACTER.`

segments.voice: The word is akhlaq: character, manners, the settled habits of a person, how they are when nobody's grading them. The hadith comes in Imam Malik's Muwatta, among other collections, and in paraphrase it says: I was sent to perfect good character. Imam Ahmad's collection has a version that says noble character. Notice the verb. Perfect. Complete. Not invent. Some readers take it to mean that good character, honesty, generosity, keeping a promise, was already known, and the Prophet came to bring it to completion. The Qur'an says of his own, in Pickthall's translation: "And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature." And when his wife Aisha was asked to describe his character, her answer in Sahih Muslim is short: his character was the Qur'an. What the book says, he was. So this block turns. The last block asked what Muslims believe. This one asks what kind of person belief makes. Muslim scholars wrote whole works on akhlaq: on patience and anger, envy and generosity, the heart's diseases and cures, and we'll walk through some of them. A hadith in Bukhari puts the measure plainly: the best of you are those who are best in character. Not the loudest, not the most learned. A measure anybody can be held to, at a checkout counter, on a crowded train, in a group chat.
screen: `AKHLAQ: WHO YOU ARE UNGRADED.` · `SENT TO PERFECT, NOT TO INVENT.` · `HIS CHARACTER WAS THE QUR'AN.` · then, large: `THE BEST OF YOU: BEST IN CHARACTER.`

segments.voice: Pick one trait you'd like to grow, patience, honesty, generosity, gentleness, keeping your word, and shrink it to something small enough to do before tonight: one true sentence where an easy one would do, letting someone go first, the call you said you'd make. Say that small act to yourself, plainly, once. If you pray, ask Allah to beautify your character in your own words; if not, simply set the intention.
Akhlaq. Character: the settled habits of a person, which the Prophet said he was sent to perfect. Today's word.
Your line: sent for character. Good character wasn't invented; he came to perfect it. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims study akhlaq, good character, as part of the faith, often starting from the hadith that the Prophet was sent to perfect good character and from accounts of his own conduct.

chat.says: What did the Prophet say he was sent for? Mostly rules?
options: In one hadith, to perfect good character; the best of you are the best in character.
To invent good manners, since nobody had known kindness or honesty before.
Only to bring rules; how you treat people was never part of his mission.
